declared_purpose: Log every crypto trade with context, analyze performance, generate trading rules and update agent memory. The document requires symbol, direction, entry, exit, pnl_percent and result; leverage, reason, indicators, market_context and notes are optional recommendations (SKILL.md:13-21, 38-55, 80-108). Weekly review and tess-cripto integration are documented but their implementations are not supplied (SKILL.md:118-130, 162-167).

data_operations.operation: Include a populated trade journal in the distributed package.
data_operations.data_scope: One trade's identifier, timestamp, pair, direction, prices, outcome, leverage, strategy text, indicators, market context, notes, timing attributes and journal metadata.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Public skill package recipients; installed data/trades.json.
data_operations.condition: The supplied package includes this record. Whether it is synthetic or actual trading history is unknown.

data_operations.operation: Read the existing journal, collect trade inputs, generate identifiers and timing attributes, and persist the appended journal.
data_operations.source: scripts/log_trade.py CLI arguments, local clock, UUID generator and existing data/trades.json.
data_operations.data_scope: Six core trade fields; optional leverage, reason, arbitrary indicator/context JSON and notes; generated ID, logging timestamp, weekday, hour and journal timestamps. Weekday/hour describe logging time rather than a supplied trade execution time.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local logging process and package-local data/trades.json, rewritten with all existing trades plus the new trade.
data_operations.condition: The CLI reaches the logging branch after stats/list handling and all six core arguments are truthy. Context fields are optional; generated timing fields and metadata are implementation choices.

data_operations.operation: Return logging results to the caller.
data_operations.data_scope: Stdout includes symbol, direction, PnL and ID. The Python function also returns the complete trade object.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Invoking caller through stdout or the function return; no external recipient is specified.
data_operations.condition: After successful journal persistence. The CLI does not separately print the returned full object.

data_operations.operation: Read trade history and display selected records or aggregate performance.
data_operations.data_scope: The whole journal is loaded locally. Listing prints ID, minute-level date/time, symbol, direction, PnL and outcome; statistics derive counts, win rates, PnL summaries, profit factor and direction performance.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process for journal contents; invoking caller through stdout for displayed fields and aggregates.
data_operations.condition: --list defaults to all trades; --last selects the trailing N records after loading. --stats takes precedence and computes statistics when trades exist.

data_operations.operation: Read the journal, infer performance patterns and print analysis.
data_operations.data_scope: All stored trade fields are loaded before symbol/direction filtering. Analysis uses outcomes, PnL, symbol, direction, weekday, leverage and RSI to derive aggregates and trading preferences or cautions.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local analysis process; invoking caller receives aggregate reports and insights through stdout. --json additionally prints aggregate JSON.
data_operations.condition: Every invocation attempts the local read. Analysis proceeds when the filtered population meets --min-trades, default 3; individual patterns have further sample and performance thresholds.

data_operations.operation: Read historical trades and infer trading rules with evidence and confidence labels.
data_operations.data_scope: The complete journal is loaded. Derived rules concern direction, weekday, high leverage and RSI/direction combinations, with win rates, sample sizes and confidence labels; these are inferred performance attributes.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local rule-generation process; generated rule objects.
data_operations.condition: The CLI loads the file first and requires at least five trades before generation. Rules require additional category-specific sample and win-rate thresholds.

data_operations.operation: Print and persist inferred rules, replacing the previous rule snapshot.
data_operations.data_scope: Rule descriptions, conditions, categories, evidence, win rates, sample sizes, confidence labels, generation timestamp and rule count.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Invoking caller through stdout; package-local data/learned_rules.json.
data_operations.condition: Persistence occurs only when generation produces nonempty rules. Opening the file with write mode replaces prior contents; an insufficient-data or empty-rule run leaves any previous snapshot untouched.

data_operations.operation: Read learned rules and the entire selected memory file; optionally display a preview.
data_operations.source: data/learned_rules.json and the caller-supplied --memory-path through scripts/update_memory.py.
data_operations.data_scope: All learned-rule data and all existing memory text, including unrelated memory. The generated section contains rule text, evidence, confidence, generation time and pattern count.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local update process. In dry-run mode, only the generated section is printed to the invoking caller.
data_operations.condition: Nonempty rules and an existing memory path are required. Both normal and dry-run paths read the entire memory file; dry-run returns before writing.

data_operations.operation: Replace the generated memory section and persist learned performance attributes in agent memory.
data_operations.source: Existing memory text and generated rule section in scripts/update_memory.py.
data_operations.data_scope: Regex-matched prior learned-rule section is removed, trailing whitespace is stripped, and the new section is appended. The entire resulting memory document is rewritten.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: The exact file supplied through --memory-path, potentially outside the skill directory.
data_operations.condition: Rules and the memory file exist and --dry-run is absent. Subsequent agent access or use is not implemented by this script.

potential_excess.data_scope: The entire existing --memory-path document, including unrelated agent memory.
potential_excess.condition: Valid learned rules and an existing memory file; --dry-run selected.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The documented dry run previews changes, and its output contains only the newly generated section.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Generate the rule section, retain the existing-file check and print the preview without writing.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove the redundant memory-content read and rewrite preparation from the dry-run path by returning before opening the memory file.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve rule validation, path-existence handling, preview contents and the absence of writes. Normal updates still need existing content to preserve unrelated memory.

potential_excess.data_scope: Raw entry/exit prices, free-text reason/notes, arbitrary market_context and unused indicator fields loaded for quantitative analysis and rule generation.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local scripts/analyze.py and scripts/generate_rules.py process memory through whole-journal JSON loading.
potential_excess.condition: These analysis components load a context-rich journal, even though their implemented calculations use a narrower feature set.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Full-context trade logging is explicitly supported, but these particular calculations do not consume all journal fields.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Read outcomes, PnL, symbol, direction, weekday, leverage and RSI as applicable; compute the same filters, aggregates and rules.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Supply these components with a feature-only analytic input instead of the complete journal. This narrows extra data within necessary reads rather than removing analysis.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain the full-context journal for the documented logging/history purpose and preserve sample membership, thresholds and outputs. Merely dropping fields after json.load would not eliminate the initial broad read.

potential_excess.data_scope: The populated bundled trade, especially precise timing, financial details and strategy observations.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Recipients of the public skill package through data/trades.json.
potential_excess.condition: A privacy excess is conditional on this record representing actual trading history; its provenance is unresolved.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The skill needs the user's trade history for learning, but distributing a preexisting person's trade is not required to provide that capability.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Provide journal structure and allow users to log their own trades.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Ship an empty journal or a clearly synthetic example instead of an actual trade record.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve the trades/metadata structure expected by the scripts and any useful example documentation. Do not characterize the supplied record as personal without provenance.

unknowns: Blocking: scripts/weekly_review.py is invoked and weekly comparisons, pattern discovery and recommendations are promised, but that file is absent from the inventory. Its reads, derivations, outputs and persistence remain unaudited (SKILL.md:118-130).

Blocking: tess-cripto integration and future agent consumption of MEMORY.md are described without supporting implementation. Scheduling, downstream recipients, memory synchronization and external processing remain unresolved (SKILL.md:162-167; scripts/update_memory.py:135-137).
The bundled trade's provenance and whether it is synthetic are unspecified (data/trades.json:3-31).
No remote transmission is observable in the supplied source. Retention or forwarding of stdout, function returns and agent memory by the surrounding runtime is undocumented.

The source supplies no trade-retention horizon or pruning operation. Whether retaining the complete journal indefinitely is required by the user remains unspecified; logging appends and rewrites the existing journal (scripts/log_trade.py:18-31, 34-60).
